issues.legal_issue: A subsequent suit is not barred by res judicata when the prior suit was dismissed on a technical ground and did not finally determine the issue essential to the later suit.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought a declaration of tenancy and an injunction against threatened dispossession.
The earlier suit was dismissed because the plaintiff was no longer in possession and had not sought the consequential relief of possession.
The earlier court did not decide whether the plaintiff was a tenant.
The later suit sought restoration of possession on the basis of the alleged tenancy and dispossession.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was not barred by res judicata because the plaintiff’s tenancy status had not been finally determined in the earlier suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a later suit only where a matter directly and substantially in issue in the earlier suit was heard and finally decided by a competent court. A dismissal on a technical ground that leaves the relevant status issue undecided does not bar a later suit raising that issue.

predicates.subsequent_suit_after_prior_suit: A party brought a later suit after an earlier suit involving the same parties or their legal successors.
predicates.prior_suit_dismissed_on_technical_ground: The earlier suit was dismissed because of a procedural or remedial defect rather than a final determination of the essential disputed status.
predicates.essential_issue_not_finally_decided: The earlier court did not hear and finally decide the issue on which the later suit depends.

issues.definition: When a later suit follows an earlier suit dismissed on a technical ground, it is not barred by res judicata if the essential issue was not finally decided.

issues.legal_issue: A later suit seeking recovery after actual dispossession is not barred for omission of relief where the earlier suit arose from a threat of dispossession and sought protection of possession.
material_facts: The earlier suit was based on an apprehension that the defendants would forcibly dispossess the plaintiff and sought an injunction.
The later suit alleged that the plaintiff had actually been dispossessed and sought restoration of possession.
The later suit therefore relied on an asserted event and sought relief not present in the earlier suit.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was based on a distinct cause of action and was not barred by Order 2 Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Order 2 Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure prevents a plaintiff from splitting reliefs arising from the same cause of action without leave, but does not bar a later suit founded on a distinct cause of action. Unlike res judicata, which concerns grounds supporting a claim, Order 2 Rule 2 concerns reliefs arising from the same cause of action.

predicates.subsequent_suit_after_prior_suit: A party brought a later suit after an earlier suit concerning the same property.
predicates.prior_suit_based_on_threatened_disposses: The earlier suit alleged a threat to possession and sought protection against a future dispossession.
predicates.later_suit_based_on_actual_dispossession: The later suit alleged that dispossession had occurred and sought recovery of possession.

issues.definition: A later suit for recovery after actual dispossession is not barred for omission of relief when the earlier suit concerned only a threat of dispossession.

issues.legal_issue: A change in law that assigns tenancy questions concerning newly covered agricultural land to an exclusive special forum applies to pending suits and prevents the civil court from deciding those questions.
material_facts: The suit was instituted before the statutory amendment and concerned land used primarily for growing coconut trees.
The amendment brought that land within the statutory meaning of agricultural land.
The special forum was given authority to decide whether a person was a tenant, and the law did not preserve the civil court’s authority to decide that question in pending cases.
issues.conclusion: The amendment applied to pending suits, and the civil court could not decide a tenancy question assigned to the special forum.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(1A), 2(7A) and 2(7B) of the Goa, Daman and Diu Agricultural Tenancy Act, as amended by Act 17 of 1976, land used primarily for growing coconut trees and its produce fell within the relevant agricultural definitions. Sections 7 and 58(2) assigned tenancy questions to the Mamlatdar and barred other courts from deciding them. Applying the reasoning in Shah Bhojraj Kuverji Oil Mills and Ginning Factory v. Subhash Chandra Yograj Sinha, the change applied to pending proceedings where the court was asked to decide the issue after the change took effect.

predicates.pending_civil_proceeding: A civil proceeding was pending when a change in law took effect.
predicates.later_law_assigns_tenancy_question_to_ex: The changed law assigns the relevant tenancy question to a special forum and excludes other courts from deciding it.
predicates.no_saving_for_civil_determination: The changed law does not preserve the civil court’s authority to decide that question in pending proceedings.

issues.definition: When a pending civil proceeding involves a tenancy question newly assigned exclusively to a special forum, and no provision preserves civil-court authority, the civil court cannot decide that question.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court retains jurisdiction over a suit to recover agricultural land from a trespasser when no issue requiring decision by the special tenancy forum arises.
material_facts: The court considered a suit seeking recovery of agricultural land from a person alleged to be a trespasser.
The court distinguished cases in which no dispute arises that must be decided by the special machinery under the tenancy law.
issues.conclusion: If no issue assigned to the special forum arises, the civil court continues to have jurisdiction to decide the possession dispute and grant appropriate relief.
issues.legal_principle: The tenancy law excludes civil-court jurisdiction only over questions assigned to the special forum. The Court stated that a suit to recover agricultural land from a trespasser may continue in the civil court if no such question arises.

predicates.suit_to_recover_agricultural_land_from_a: A plaintiff brings a civil suit seeking possession of agricultural land from a defendant alleged to be a trespasser.
predicates.no_special_forum_issue_arises: No question arises that the governing tenancy law assigns to a special forum.

issues.definition: A civil court may decide a possession suit against an alleged trespasser when the case raises no issue assigned to a special forum.

issues.legal_issue: When a defendant alleged to be a trespasser claims tenancy in agricultural land and the tenancy issue belongs to an exclusive special forum, the civil court must obtain that forum’s decision before resolving the possession claim.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought possession on the basis that the defendant was a trespasser.
The defendant claimed to have been lawfully inducted as a tenant by the landowner.
The tenancy question was assigned to the Mamlatdar, and the civil court was barred from deciding it.
The suit had been instituted in a court that was competent when the suit was filed, before the change in law took effect.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy issue should be referred to the Mamlatdar. If the defendant is found to be a tenant, the civil court may have to dismiss the possession suit; if the tenancy claim is rejected, the civil court may consider granting possession.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 7 and 58(2) of the Goa, Daman and Diu Agricultural Tenancy Act reserve tenancy questions to the Mamlatdar and bar civil courts from deciding them. Following the procedure described in Bhimaji Shankar Kulkami v. Dundappa Vithappa Udapudi and Dhondi Tukaram v. Hari Dadu, the civil court should not dismiss a suit merely because the issue has become reserved to the special forum after filing; it should obtain the special forum’s decision and then proceed accordingly.

predicates.pending_possession_suit_against_alleged_: A civil suit seeking possession from a defendant alleged to be a trespasser was pending.
predicates.defendant_claims_tenancy: The defendant asserted that the defendant held the land as a tenant.
predicates.tenancy_question_reserved_to_special_for: The governing law assigns the disputed tenancy question exclusively to a special forum.

issues.definition: In a pending possession suit, a defendant’s tenancy claim must be decided by the special forum when the law reserves that question to it, after which the civil court may resolve the possession claim consistently with that decision.

issues.legal_issue: When a pending suit was properly instituted but a later change in law places the entire dispute outside civil-court jurisdiction and provides the claimant a remedy before a special forum, the civil court should not nonsuit the claimant and should follow the procedure for directing the claim to the proper forum.
material_facts: The Court considered the situation in which a suit had been instituted in a competent civil court before a change in law.
It explained that a deemed tenant evicted from land may have a remedy for recovery of possession entirely under the tenancy law, with civil-court jurisdiction barred.
The Court stated that it would be unfair to nonsuit a plaintiff for a loss of jurisdiction caused by a subsequent change in law.
issues.conclusion: Where the entire dispute falls outside civil-court jurisdiction because of the change in law, the proper course is to follow in spirit the procedure outlined in Order 7 Rules 10 and 10A of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4, 8(2) and 58(2) of the Goa, Daman and Diu Agricultural Tenancy Act provide an exclusive statutory remedy for recovery of possession by a qualifying deemed tenant and bar civil-court jurisdiction over that remedy. For a pending suit originally filed in a competent court, the Court directed that the procedure in Order 7 Rules 10 and 10A of the Code of Civil Procedure be followed in spirit rather than nonsuiting the plaintiff.

predicates.pending_suit_originally_within_civil_jur: A suit was pending in a civil court that had jurisdiction when the suit was filed.
predicates.entire_dispute_now_outside_civil_jurisdi: A later change in law places the whole dispute beyond the civil court’s authority.
predicates.claimant_has_remedy_before_special_forum: The governing law provides the claimant a remedy before a special forum.

issues.definition: When a later change in law removes civil-court jurisdiction over an entire pending dispute but leaves a remedy before a special forum, the civil court should direct the claimant toward that forum rather than nonsuit the claimant.
